questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.topic: 1914 and 1945 read as a pair
questions.learningObjective: Compare 1914 and 1945 as a paired marker
questions.stem: Note 2101 records 1914 and 1945 as a pair of markers for one long conflict.

options.text: 1914 opens the crisis and 1945 closes its second phase, so the pair frames one long conflict.
1914 and 1945 are interchangeable labels for the same war.
1945 makes 1914 irrelevant to European order.
Only 1914 matters because it started everything.

questions.explanation: 1914 and 1945 work as a pair because the first opens the crisis and the second closes its second phase. The error is to collapse them into one war or to discard the earlier date.
questions.hint: Pair the opening and closing dates.

questions.topic: Ordering a causal chain of institutions

options.text: The later institution always causes the earlier one.
Causes must be ordered so each step precedes and enables the next.

questions.explanation: A causal chain of institutions must run in chronological order, with each step enabling the next. The error is to reverse or randomise the sequence.
